h1: Land Rover DC-DC Converter Repair (Ingenium MHEV)
lede: Specialist replacement of the 48V to 12V DC-DC converter on Land Rover Ingenium mild-hybrid vehicles. Full JLR diagnostics, high-voltage safety procedures, and genuine parts.

sections.heading: What the DC-DC Converter Repair Involves

blocks.html: The DC-DC converter is a critical component of the 48-volt mild-hybrid system on Land Rover Ingenium MHEV vehicles. It converts 48V to 12V, powering the standard electrical systems including lights, infotainment, and engine control modules. When the converter fails, the entire 12V electrical system can shut down — sometimes while driving.
Our workshop specialises in the safe, precise replacement of this component. Every job follows strict high-voltage safety procedures and uses JLR-specific diagnostic equipment to verify the repair.

paras: Includes genuine Land Rover DC-DC converter, high-voltage safety procedures, JLR diagnostics, and full system testing. [Pricing disclaimer](/pricing-legal-disclaimer)

steps.title: Safety & Preparation
steps.body: Ignition off, key removed, 12V battery disconnected, 48V system isolated. Vehicle placed in a workshop bay with high-voltage safety protocols in place.

steps.title: Access & Removal
steps.body: DC-DC converter located (position varies by model). Mounting bolts removed, electrical connections (48V and 12V circuits) disconnected, converter removed.

steps.title: Installation
steps.body: New genuine Land Rover DC-DC converter fitted to mounting bracket. Electrical connections reconnected, bolts torqued to specification.

steps.title: Re-energisation & Testing
steps.body: 12V battery reconnected, 48V system re-energised. JLR-specific diagnostic equipment verifies correct operation and charging system health.

items.q: What is the DC-DC converter on a Land Rover Ingenium MHEV?
items.a: The DC-DC converter is a critical component of the 48-volt mild-hybrid system. It converts 48V to 12V to power the vehicle's standard 12V electrical systems, including lights, infotainment, and engine control modules.

items.q: How do I know if my Land Rover needs a DC-DC converter replacement?
items.a: Common symptoms include complete loss of 12V electrical power (sometimes while driving), warning lights on the dashboard, and charging system faults. Our workshop uses JLR-specific diagnostics to confirm the fault.

items.q: Which Land Rover models are affected by DC-DC converter failure?
items.a: The DC-DC converter is fitted to Ingenium MHEV variants including: Defender (D200, D250, D300, D350, P400), Discovery (D250, D300, D350, P400), Discovery Sport (D200), Range Rover (D300/D350, P400), Range Rover Sport (D300, P400), Range Rover Velar (D250, D300, P400), and Range Rover Evoque (D200). Non-MHEV variants and the Defender Octa are not affected.

items.q: Do I need to use a genuine Land Rover DC-DC converter?
items.a: Yes. The only reliable repair is replacement with a new, genuine Land Rover DC-DC converter. Aftermarket or used parts may not function correctly with the vehicle's MHEV system and can cause recurring faults.

items.q: How long does a DC-DC converter replacement take?
items.a: The replacement typically takes 3–5 hours, including system de-energisation, removal, installation, and full JLR diagnostic testing. The exact duration depends on the specific model and access to the converter.

items.q: Do you offer a warranty on the replacement?
items.a: All DC-DC converter replacements are covered by our standard 12-month, unlimited-mileage warranty. [Learn more about our warranty](/landrover-engine-warranty).
